questions.q: Find the equation of the line passing through $A(2, -3)$ and $B(6, 5)$ in the form $y = mx + c$.
Find the length of the line segment joining $P(-1, 4)$ and $Q(5, -4)$.
Find the midpoint of the segment connecting $C(-3, 8)$ and $D(7, -2)$.
Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $A(1, 2)$ and $B(5, 10)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint $M = (3, 6)$. Gradient of $AB = \frac{10 - 2}{5 - 1} = 2$. Perpendicular gradient $m_\perp = -1/2$. Equation: $y - 6 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 3) \Rightarrow 2y - 12 = -x + 3 \Rightarrow x + 2y = 15$.

questions.q: The line $L_1$ has equation $3x - 4y = 12$. Find the equation of the line $L_2$ perpendicular to $L_1$ passing through $(2, 1)$.
questions.answer: Slope of $L_1$ is $3/4$. Perpendicular slope is $-4/3$. Equation: $y - 1 = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 2) \Rightarrow 3y - 3 = -4x + 8 \Rightarrow 4x + 3y = 11$.

questions.q: Three points are given: $P(1, 1)$, $Q(4, 5)$, and $R(k, 9)$. If $P, Q, R$ are collinear, find $k$.
Find the center and radius of the circle given by $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y - 11 = 0$.
Find the equation of the tangent to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 25$ at the point $(3, 4)$.
questions.answer: The radius to $(3, 4)$ has gradient $4/3$. Tangent is perpendicular, with gradient $-3/4$. Equation: $y - 4 = -\frac{3}{4}(x - 3) \Rightarrow 4y - 16 = -3x + 9 \Rightarrow 3x + 4y = 25$.

questions.q: A circle has diameter with endpoints $A(-2, 1)$ and $B(4, 9)$. Find the equation of the circle.
Determine the relationship between the line $y = x - 5$ and the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 9$.
choices: The line does not intersect the circle
The line is tangent to the circle
The line intersects the circle in two distinct points
The line passes through the center of the circle
questions.answer: Substitute: $x^2 + (x - 5)^2 = 9 \Rightarrow 2x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - 5x + 8 = 0$. $\Delta = 25 - 32 = -7 < 0$. No real solutions, so no intersection.

questions.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(0, 0)$, $B(6, 2)$, and $C(2, 8)$.
Find the length of the chord cut off from the line $y = 2$ by the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 13$.
questions.answer: Set $y = 2$: $x^2 + 4 = 13 \Rightarrow x^2 = 9 \Rightarrow x = \pm 3$. The points are $(-3, 2)$ and $(3, 2)$, so chord length is $3 - (-3) = 6$.
